newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market moved higher on Wednesday, bouncing back with Italian bonds, but dealers said the recovery will prove short-lived.
"The underlying tone is still negative. It's true that we have a pretty good rise today, but we didn't see much buying around here," a dealer with a U.S. house in Madrid said.
"Domestic investors are at the window, looking for cheaper buying, while foreigners stay out," another dealer added.
Fears over possible delays in the EMU project were scaring most, with a likely U.S. FOMC rate hike looming on the horizon, traders said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds fell to 128 basis points from 135 bps at the close on Tuesday.
The yield curve was little changed, though dealers were reporting massive selling in the three-to-five-year segment.
"These maturities are the ones everybody was buying when Euro-optimism was at its height in January," a dealer said.
"So these maturities are the ones people sell now without any regard to the yield curve," another added.
